page: OVHcloud r3-64-flex is a memory-optimized cloud server deployed on KVM virtualization, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated physical cores configured with 1 thread per core, providing 8 total vCPUs without symmetric multiprocessing. The CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets.

The hardware configuration features 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and networking throughput is rated at a 2 Gbps baseline. No hardware accelerators are present on this instance, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory subsystems and single-threaded execution. PassMark memory testing scored 2970.4, ranking in the top 25%, paired with an uncached memory write bandwidth of 101.45 GB/sec. Stress-ng single-core performance achieved 3077.58, while Geekbench multi-core scored 9854.0 and PassMark CPU scored 20373.07. Redis SET operations measured 18.96 million operations per second, and text processing in Geekbench scored 2628.0.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective resource profile for workloads requiring substantial volatile memory without paying for excessive core allocations. While local storage is limited to 50 GB NVMe, the high memory density and dedicated core allocation make the r3-64-flex well positioned for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed ETL batch jobs, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: OVHcloud r3-64-flex is a memory-optimized server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz on KVM virtualization. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, 64 GB of system memory at an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a 2 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic tests indicate strong single-core and memory throughput, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 2970.4 and large-block write bandwidth of 101.45 GB/sec. General compute metrics show a PassMark CPU score of 20373.07 and 18.96 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers cost efficiency by pairing high RAM capacity with modest compute and local storage footprints, making it suitable for in-memory caching tiers, database workloads, and data pipelines.
